approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a live population of scored molecular graphs. It samples parents from high-scoring bands, generates offspring through crossover or short sequences of atom and bond mutations, and fills a fresh pool with valid, novel identities. Only the final product of each ordinary mutation sequence is offered to that pool. A Gaussian-process predictor fitted to all real accepted scores uses folded local count fingerprints and correlated posterior draws to select the evaluation batch. Newly accepted offspring enter the full score archive and compete for the score-greedy survivor population, allowing useful descendants to become later parents. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled; identity checks, continuation, retries and crossover finishing mutation remain active.
approach.novelty: Make successful intermediate products of ordinary mutation sequences available to the existing pool selector. Finish the entire original sequence, offer its final product first, then offer earlier successful products from latest to earliest under the same validity and novelty gates. This preserves continuation while exposing molecules it currently passes over. It differs from shortening mutation sequences, adding a new graph move, changing breeding preference or rewarding unscored intermediates. Intermediate products occupy some slots that would otherwise require independent final proposals, so increased path coverage can help or hurt the complete search.

hypothesis: After each complete inherited ordinary single-parent mutation chain, offer its original final product first and then its proper successful graph snapshots in reverse chronological order to the same bounded novel-candidate pool, without shortening or extending the chain.

finding_summary.headline: Harvested prefixes reached real feedback and breeding, but the paired mean endpoint fell by 0.040930
finding_summary.insights:
Making earlier products visible can expose useful molecules without improving the overall search. Among 49 same-attempt pairs where both prefix and final were actually scored, prefixes won 34, lost ten and tied five. These selected, dependent comparisons do not describe all intermediates. The only prefix that first attained a session endpoint was a zaleplon product whose original final remained unscored; that session still finished below its matched Parent. Across the whole Child, parent wins rose from 629 to 722 and incumbent advances from 258 to 306, yet the complete endpoint mean declined. The retained GP also had lower error on its changed evaluated stream, which cannot establish a better model or explain the loss.

The result applies to this one final-first/reverse-prefix collection rule. Prefix occupancy, fewer independent attempts and later adaptive histories changed together, so their separate effects remain unresolved. It does not reverse the earlier positive contribution of retaining ordinary continuation or justify assuming shallower products are better. Chemical counterexamples reinforce that boundary: a higher-scoring prefix retains an acyl fluoride, while another oxygen-ring prefix loses substantially to its sulfur-ring final. Conventional indole amides and useful aryl amines coexist with reactive bonds, excessive elaboration, difficult rings and unspecified stereochemistry. Extra path coverage did not establish chemical feasibility or independent scaffold coverage. Higher-floor recovery and mutation-call exhaustion were tested only in isolated controls, not naturally exercised here.
finding_summary.results: The full inherited mutation chains ran, and 7,287 proper intermediate products entered the fixed pools. Of 461 evaluated prefixes, 78 beat their generating parent, 353 lost and 30 tied; 29 advanced the incumbent. After feedback, 370 survived their batch and 294 later bred in 10,630 actual parent draws. All 435 pools filled. Multiple admissions reduced independent generation attempts from 75,961 to 67,373, without shortening any completed chain. All three matched replicas completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.554740, a paired loss of 0.040930 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed changes were −0.089537, +0.003553 and −0.036805. Four task/seed endpoints improved—zaleplon seed 0, drd2 and sitagliptin seed 1, and median_2 seed 2—while eleven declined. The mechanism is confirmed and its endpoint-benefit prediction is falsified.

molecular.headline: Indole amides and aryl amines coexist with reactive halogens, oversized heterocycles and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were read, covering Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 with 300 observations per task/seed. The fresh brief marks complete Child evaluation and complete matched pairing to n-62daf219c70a, with no profile mismatch or missing trajectory. Each task has 900 records, including 870 evaluated optimizer proposals. The digest counters describe those evaluated proposals, not every unscored pool molecule or intermediate graph. Their ring-closure text incidence is 0.9655 to 0.9862 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9598 to 0.9816; charge and stereocentre text incidence are zero throughout. These incidences do not count perceived rings, aromatic-atom fractions, stereoisomers or protonation states. Sizes below are heavy-atom-token counts from the actual SMILES. The output includes compact indole amides, amidines, aryl aminoalkyl compounds, medium nitrogen rings, crowded fused nitrogen-carbonyl systems and extensively linked ester/imine/heterocyclic assemblies. Ring chemistry and aromaticity are rich. Synthetic plausibility is questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because recognizable compounds coexist with N-halogen, O-F/O-Cl, acyl-halide, peroxide and unusual sulfur multiple-bond environments, difficult bridges and excessive elaboration. Diversity is moderate across tasks/seeds and narrower among each seed's leaders; there is no basis to equate extra path positions with independent scaffold diversity. Every accepted offspring was joined by session, batch and emitted identity to its actual pool role and earlier scored parents: 4,350 joins comprise 2,429 ordinary finals, 1,460 crossover finals and 461 proper prefixes. Full ordinary effort comes only from 37,238 ordinary_mutation_chain records: 44,942 mutate calls and 56,618 inner attempts. Per-product traces overlap or truncate these chains and must not be summed as additional effort. There are 7,704 successful proper intermediate positions from 6,620 chains; 7,287 enter the fixed pools, while 362 are duplicates, 3 invalid and 52 overflow. Only 461 pool-admitted prefixes are evaluated. Among them, 374 have immediate survivor-admission receipts, 78 beat their generating parent and 29 advance the incumbent. Later accepted-descendant records reuse 157 as parents; this is observed-parent reuse, not an exhaustive count of all breeding draws. Immediate admission is not permanent retention. The earliest molecule attaining each final session-best score is a crossover final in seven sessions, ordinary final in seven and proper prefix in one. Later tied endpoint molecules can have different roles, including a proper-prefix amidine. No natural higher-floor ordinary chain or stopped-on-failure chain appears in the audited panel; synthetic implementation controls are not outcome evidence for those cases. There are 49 same-attempt prefix/final pairings where both products received real labels: 34 prefixes score higher, 10 lower and 5 tie. These selected, dependent pairings are not an estimate over all intermediates and do not identify the overall intervention's benefit. The per-task examples retain both directions. Unselected intermediate or final products have no counterfactual score here. A successful graph step, admission, parent win or ancestry is not proof of chemical improvement. One prior snapshot's checked serialization differs from its later admitted text; the audit retains that distinction and joins the stable normalized admission, emission and accepted identity instead of treating raw text difference as a new molecule. The extra path products share scored generating parents; unscored intermediates are not assigned parent labels. The matched Parent already expresses the inherited chemistry gaps originating in n-c55c3d520a2c. This Child's pool composition, ordinary generation effort and later adaptive history change together; chemical observations do not separate these effects. The earlier continuation-removal first products described by the immutable brief belong to that different history and provide no labels for current or Parent-unselected prefixes. Shared-Parent siblings are not independent replications or additive component effects. The reported raw scores do not establish synthesis, stability, biological activity, global calibration or causal mediation. The digest's final excerpt contains late seed-2 proposals, not every retained leader. This report makes no activation, eligibility, Anchor or stage decision. Reproducible trajectory and accepted-role audits are under runs/SPIRAL2/.slots/r0020-00-improve-L01/molecular/.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c, was reproduced in n-62daf219c70a, and is re-observed with different molecules in n-79bc7a1dd0dc on the complete matched three-Search-Seed panel at 300 observations per task. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments around useful aromatic and heterocyclic arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need environment-sensitive alternatives that preserve favorable structural relationships learned from real feedback. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens and useful amines from reactive heteroatom-halogen or acyl-halide bonds. These associations motivate chemistry assessment, not a universal filter, a presumed score benefit or attribution of the liabilities to prefix admission.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The n-c55c3d520a2c/n-62daf219c70a gap concerned cyclic unsaturation and bridges. Current n-79bc7a1dd0dc molecules include crowded O/N bridges, large aromatic-labelled nitrogen regions, medium nitrogen-dicarbonyl rings, fused stereogenic centres and a substituted cyclobutene. Ring-text incidence remains high at 0.9655 to 0.9862. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently separate representable ring connectivity from plausible geometry and accessible synthesis.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring edits need context about ring size, unsaturation, junction geometry and plausible alternative connectivities. Preserve useful rings while checking their feasibility rather than treating aromatic labels, path depth or successful graph validation as sufficient. No specific ring filter or geometric mechanism is shown to improve the objective by this chemistry assessment.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was present in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a and persists in n-79bc7a1dd0dc under the matched panel. transferable_gaps.gap: The generated output leaves potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged environments unspecified.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly resolve chemically relevant stereochemical identity during generation, while handling protonation and tautomerism separately. Account for achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Additional admitted path products do not supply missing stereochemical definition, and the observations do not measure a stereochemical score penalty or identify a component cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This conditional gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c/n-62daf219c70a and recurs in n-79bc7a1dd0dc: late tiny fragments reach observed floors, while an 87-heavy-atom assembly scores below its seed's 68-atom leader and a 54-atom linked carbonyl-rich molecule has a near-zero score. A compact 24-atom indole amide and a 26-atom carbon-fluorinated nitrogen-dione leader show that useful output need not be large. transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful functional context while avoiding fragmentation and excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local accepted feedback and chemical context to preserve useful functional relationships during simplification, extension or replacement. Do not infer chemical quality from an intermediate position, prescribe a fixed minimum size, or assume shorter paths are preferable. The observed selected pairs cannot label omitted intermediates or isolate prefix quality from changed pool composition, effort and later adaptive history.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading-family coverage gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c/n-62daf219c70a and remains conditional on this finite n-79bc7a1dd0dc panel. Leaders and ties repeatedly alter halogens, short side chains, local heteroatoms or ring segments on retained aromatic amide, amidine, aryl-amine and nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks. Different seeds do form different families, so diversity is moderate rather than globally collapsed. The 7,287 pool-admitted prefixes share their actual generating parents and chains; only 461 have accepted labels. Extra positions and distinct strings therefore do not establish useful independent chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently provide independent plausible scaffold alternatives within each seed’s leading chemical family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore feasible alternative connectivities that preserve structural relationships supported by real task-local feedback, and assess actual chemical and score outcomes separately from path coverage. Retain the counterexamples and original Parent conditions. This does not establish a universal diversity benefit, independent replication of shared-Parent histories, an additive mechanism effect or justification to assign scores to unobserved prefixes.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a live population of scored molecular graphs. It samples parents from high-scoring bands, generates offspring through crossover or short sequences of atom and bond mutations, and fills a fresh pool with valid, novel identities. Only the final product of each ordinary mutation sequence is offered to that pool. A Gaussian-process predictor fitted to all real accepted scores uses folded local count fingerprints and correlated posterior draws to select the evaluation batch. Newly accepted offspring enter the full score archive and compete for the score-greedy survivor population, allowing useful descendants to become later parents. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled; identity checks, continuation, retries and crossover finishing mutation remain active.
approach.novelty: Make successful intermediate products of ordinary mutation sequences available to the existing pool selector. Finish the entire original sequence, offer its final product first, then offer earlier successful products from latest to earliest under the same validity and novelty gates. This preserves continuation while exposing molecules it currently passes over. It differs from shortening mutation sequences, adding a new graph move, changing breeding preference or rewarding unscored intermediates. Intermediate products occupy some slots that would otherwise require independent final proposals, so increased path coverage can help or hurt the complete search.

The two terminal-best sessions with relocation ancestry both have lower paired endpoints, and their ancestral positional products originally tied or lost. Subsequent crossover and mutation prevent treating that ancestry as conserved-group mediation. The largest positive task-seed change occurs in a cell with no evaluated relocation descendant.

Expanding the menu also changes the probabilities of legacy edits and later adaptive search, so the negative conditional result belongs to the whole menu addition, not an isolated estimate for each move. finding_summary.headline: Harvested prefixes reached real feedback and breeding, but the paired mean endpoint fell by 0.040930
finding_summary.insights:
Making earlier products visible can expose useful molecules without improving the overall search. Among 49 same-attempt pairs where both prefix and final were actually scored, prefixes won 34, lost ten and tied five. These selected, dependent comparisons do not describe all intermediates. The only prefix that first attained a session endpoint was a zaleplon product whose original final remained unscored; that session still finished below its matched Parent. Across the whole Child, parent wins rose from 629 to 722 and incumbent advances from 258 to 306, yet the complete endpoint mean declined. The retained GP also had lower error on its changed evaluated stream, which cannot establish a better model or explain the loss.

The result applies to this one final-first/reverse-prefix collection rule. Prefix occupancy, fewer independent attempts and later adaptive histories changed together, so their separate effects remain unresolved. It does not reverse the earlier positive contribution of retaining ordinary continuation or justify assuming shallower products are better. Chemical counterexamples reinforce that boundary: a higher-scoring prefix retains an acyl fluoride, while another oxygen-ring prefix loses substantially to its sulfur-ring final. Conventional indole amides and useful aryl amines coexist with reactive bonds, excessive elaboration, difficult rings and unspecified stereochemistry. Extra path coverage did not establish chemical feasibility or independent scaffold coverage. Higher-floor recovery and mutation-call exhaustion were tested only in isolated controls, not naturally exercised here.
finding_summary.results: The full inherited mutation chains ran, and 7,287 proper intermediate products entered the fixed pools. Of 461 evaluated prefixes, 78 beat their generating parent, 353 lost and 30 tied; 29 advanced the incumbent. After feedback, 370 survived their batch and 294 later bred in 10,630 actual parent draws. All 435 pools filled. Multiple admissions reduced independent generation attempts from 75,961 to 67,373, without shortening any completed chain. All three matched replicas completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.554740, a paired loss of 0.040930 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed changes were −0.089537, +0.003553 and −0.036805. Four task/seed endpoints improved—zaleplon seed 0, drd2 and sitagliptin seed 1, and median_2 seed 2—while eleven declined. The mechanism is confirmed and its endpoint-benefit prediction is falsified.

Immediate conservation has a specific boundary. Thirty-four evaluated descendants retain the complete moved branch. In the remaining case a later mutation turns the moved ethyl ester into an ethynyl ester: the attachment remains, but its internal chemistry changes. The two terminal-best sessions with relocation ancestry both have lower paired endpoints, and their ancestral positional products originally tied or lost. Subsequent crossover and mutation prevent treating that ancestry as conserved-group mediation. The largest positive task-seed change occurs in a cell with no evaluated relocation descendant.

Expanding the menu also changes the probabilities of legacy edits and later adaptive search, so the negative conditional result belongs to the whole menu addition, not an isolated estimate for each move. The molecular report finds preserved reactive groups, difficult ring arrangements and unspecified stereochemistry alongside recognizable amines, esters and lactams. Formula preservation does not fix those liabilities. finding_summary.headline: Harvested prefixes reached real feedback and breeding, but the paired mean endpoint fell by 0.040930
finding_summary.insights:
Making earlier products visible can expose useful molecules without improving the overall search. Among 49 same-attempt pairs where both prefix and final were actually scored, prefixes won 34, lost ten and tied five. These selected, dependent comparisons do not describe all intermediates. The only prefix that first attained a session endpoint was a zaleplon product whose original final remained unscored; that session still finished below its matched Parent. Across the whole Child, parent wins rose from 629 to 722 and incumbent advances from 258 to 306, yet the complete endpoint mean declined. The retained GP also had lower error on its changed evaluated stream, which cannot establish a better model or explain the loss.

The result applies to this one final-first/reverse-prefix collection rule. Prefix occupancy, fewer independent attempts and later adaptive histories changed together, so their separate effects remain unresolved. It does not reverse the earlier positive contribution of retaining ordinary continuation or justify assuming shallower products are better. Chemical counterexamples reinforce that boundary: a higher-scoring prefix retains an acyl fluoride, while another oxygen-ring prefix loses substantially to its sulfur-ring final. Conventional indole amides and useful aryl amines coexist with reactive bonds, excessive elaboration, difficult rings and unspecified stereochemistry. Extra path coverage did not establish chemical feasibility or independent scaffold coverage. Higher-floor recovery and mutation-call exhaustion were tested only in isolated controls, not naturally exercised here.
finding_summary.results: The full inherited mutation chains ran, and 7,287 proper intermediate products entered the fixed pools. Of 461 evaluated prefixes, 78 beat their generating parent, 353 lost and 30 tied; 29 advanced the incumbent. After feedback, 370 survived their batch and 294 later bred in 10,630 actual parent draws. All 435 pools filled. Multiple admissions reduced independent generation attempts from 75,961 to 67,373, without shortening any completed chain. All three matched replicas completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.554740, a paired loss of 0.040930 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed changes were −0.089537, +0.003553 and −0.036805. Four task/seed endpoints improved—zaleplon seed 0, drd2 and sitagliptin seed 1, and median_2 seed 2—while eleven declined. The mechanism is confirmed and its endpoint-benefit prediction is falsified.
